# Building HTML {#chp:html}

You do not need a template engine to produce a bit of HTML. You need to get
the escaping right, and that is where most of the trouble lives. The recipes in
this chapter build tags safely, escape what needs escaping, strip tags when you
want plain text back, and embed files in a page.

## Build and check HTML {#sec:grp-html-build}

Create tags, escape text, strip markup, and preview the result.

### Build a tag from R {#sec:html-tag}

`html_tag()` builds one tag, with attributes and content. Attributes are passed
as named arguments:

```{r}
html_tag("a", "R Project", href = "https://www.r-project.org", target = "_blank")
html_tag("br")
html_tag("p", list("Visit ", html_tag("a", "CRAN", href = "https://cran.r-project.org")))
```

Content is escaped by default, so a stray `<` in your text stays a `<`. When a
piece of content is already valid HTML and you do not want it escaped again,
wrap it in `html_value()`:

```{r}
html_tag("p", html_value("<em>already escaped</em>"))
```

### Escape text for HTML {#sec:html-escape}

When you build HTML by pasting strings together, `html_escape()` replaces `&`,
`<`, and `>`. Set `attr = TRUE` when the text goes inside an attribute, so
quotes and line breaks are escaped too:

```{r}
html_escape('2 < 3 & "quotes"')
html_escape('attr="val"', attr = TRUE)
```

### Strip tags and comments {#sec:strip-html}

Sometimes you have HTML and want only the text. `strip_html()` removes tags and
comments and leaves the words behind:

```{r}
strip_html('<p>Hello <strong>world</strong><!-- comment -->!</p>')
```

### Preview HTML in a browser {#sec:html-view}

To check how a snippet looks, `html_view()` serves it from a temporary local web
server and opens it in the browser or the RStudio viewer. It is meant for
interactive use:

```r
html_view(html_tag('h1', 'Hello', style = 'color: tomato'))
```

Relative resources (images, stylesheets) are looked up in the working
directory.

## Embed downloads {#sec:grp-html-embed}

Let readers download files from a self-contained HTML page.

### Offer a folder as a download {#sec:embed-dir}

In an HTML report, you can let readers download a whole folder without hosting
anything. `embed_dir()` zips the directory and inlines the archive as a base64
link:

```r
d = tempfile()
dir.create(d)
write.csv(head(cars), file.path(d, 'cars.csv'))
embed_dir(d, text = 'Download the data')
```

The result is an `<a download>` tag, so put it in a chunk with
`results = 'asis'` or print it in the document. Zipping needs the `zip` command
(Rtools on Windows).

### Offer several files as one download {#sec:embed-files}

For a handful of files that do not share a folder, `embed_files()` zips them
into a single archive. Pick the download name with `name`:

```r
f = c('data.csv', 'notes.txt')
embed_files(f, name = 'materials.zip')
```

For one file, use `embed_file()` directly: it skips the zip step.
